# Eodem Sensu: Sources of Catholic Dogma

> Eodem sensu, "in the same sense": the rule of Vincent of Lérins, quoted by Vatican I, that doctrine develops only in the same dogma, the same sense and the same meaning.

> Denzinger's Enchiridion in English (older numbering) from the creeds to Pius XII, and the documents of the Church from John XXIII to Leo XIV, with each text labelled by the kind of document it comes from and many graded by hand.

## Data

- [entries.json](https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/data/entries.json): every entry: id, text, DS numbers, era, year, weight (kind of document), hand-checked grade with its reason, censure, cross-references.
- [documents.json](https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/data/documents.json): source inventory, local coverage, provenance, review status and full-text links. An excerpt view is not a complete document.
- [weights.csv](https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/data/weights.csv): the hand-checked grades and the reason for each.
- [latin.json](https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/data/latin.json): the Latin text by DS number.
- [guides.json](https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/data/guides.json): the disputed questions, the guide to documents since 1950, the doctrinal threads, and the principles of hermeneutics.
- [continuity.json](https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/data/continuity.json): the hermeneutic of ecclesial continuity, a research layer: principles P1-P8 and 24 cases with propositions, contradiction matrices, provisional verdicts and evidence gaps. Not Church teaching.
- A page for each entry: https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/n/<id>/

## Citing

Before 1958, cite by the older Denzinger number: n. 1839. After 1958, by document and article: LG 25, EV 62, CCC 2267; addresses by date: AD 19641203. Each entry gives its source.

## Weight

The weight label says what kind of document a text comes from: a conciliar definition, papal teaching, a document of the Doctrine of the Faith, an address or homily, an interview (private opinion, not magisterial), a commission study, and so on. A hand-checked grade, where present, says what the text itself proposes: defined dogma, definitive, authoritative teaching, discipline, prudential judgment, or weight disputed.

## Reading magisterial texts (hermeneutics)

- Understanding of revealed truth grows, but always in the same dogma, the same sense and the same meaning; a dogma once declared is never given a different meaning.
- First ask what kind of act a text is and what assent it asks: faith for what is proposed as revealed, firm acceptance for what is proposed definitively, religious submission of mind and will for authentic teaching, obedience for discipline.
- A definition binds in what it proposes to be held; the arguments, illustrations and history around it do not share its weight.
- A magisterial text usually confirms what is contained in Scripture and Tradition while answering a particular question or error; the question it answers is part of its meaning.
- The truths a dogmatic formula teaches are distinct from the changeable conceptions of an epoch, and the formulas remain true and suitable for those who read them rightly; historical conditioning never makes a definition false.
- Read each truth in its coherence with the others and with the whole plan of revelation; truths are ordered by their relation to the foundation of the faith, which ranks them but excludes none.
- In faith and morals the true sense of Scripture is the one the Church has held and holds, never against the unanimous consent of the Fathers; the Magisterium is not above the word of God but serves it.
- Distinguish the principle a text teaches from its application to the circumstances of the time; prudential and disciplinary judgments can be revised while the principle stands.
- A condemned proposition is rejected in a determinate sense, established from its source and the wording of the condemnation; rejecting it does not define its unrestricted opposite.
- Interviews, press conferences and private writings are not acts of the Magisterium; addresses and homilies teach with the weight of their form and context.

## Reading condemned propositions

- A condemnation targets a proposition in a determinate sense, not every meaning its words could bear. Establish that sense from the source the proposition was taken from, the wording of the condemnation (named senses, censures), and authoritative explanations; never supply an intention the evidence does not show.
- With censures given respectively or in globo, each proposition deserves at least one of the listed censures, not necessarily the gravest; condemned is not the same as declared heretical.
- Rejecting a proposition in a sense does not affirm its unrestricted opposite.
- The same words can express different doctrines; a definition is what is proposed to be held, not the reasoning around it.
- An apparent contradiction between texts is a question to examine with these distinctions, not a refutation. See https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/#reading

## Hermeneutic of ecclesial continuity (research layer)

This is a research layer written for this site. It applies a published method to disputed texts and records where the method succeeds, where it fails and where the evidence is not yet in. Its verdicts, confidence levels and the proposed synthesis on Constance, Basel and Vatican I are scholarly hypotheses, not teaching of the Catholic Church and not a judgment of any office of the Holy See.

Guide: https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/#continuity · data: https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/data/continuity.json · listening scripts: https://jcalepos146.github.io/denzinger/data/continuity-audio.md

Principles P1–P8:
- P1 Logical and propositional precision: Extract the exact subject, predicate, scope, modal force, qualifications, time and object of each claim. P and not-P conflict only when asserted in the same sense and circumstances; two time-bounded commands can differ without asserting contradictory universal doctrines.
- P2 Documentary priority and competence: Identify original language, critical text, date, promulgator, session, procedural status, confirmation, reception and repeal. Inclusion in Denzinger or omission from it is editorial evidence, not a doctrinal ruling.
- P3 Formal-object differentiation: Tag each claim as revealed doctrine, definitive doctrine, authentic non-definitive teaching, juridical norm, pastoral determination, moral application, judicial sentence, dogmatic fact, historical assertion or private opinion. One act can mix several.
- P4 Proportionate assent and obligation: Distinguish divine and Catholic faith, definitive assent, religious submission of mind and will, legal obedience and prudential deference. Binding force, factual correctness, doctrinal truth and irreformability are four different properties.
- P5 Contingent determination under permanent authority: The divinely instituted power to bind and loose can ground real obligations that are neither uniquely best nor permanent (Aquinas's determinatio, applied by analogy). No human law can abrogate divine law. The analogy of an executive order illuminates governance, not the truth of competing doctrinal propositions.
- P6 Homogeneous development: Show how a later clarification or qualification keeps the earlier definitive truth. Context must come from historical evidence; an exception may not be inserted simply because a contradiction would otherwise remain.
- P7 Indefectibility, infallibility and safety: Infallibility operates under defined conditions; indefectibility keeps the Church in the apostolic faith and constitution. A wider doctrinal safety (securitas doctrinalis) for non-definitive teaching is a theological theory, not a defined grade of the Magisterium. Donum Veritatis 23–31 admits limitations and deficiencies in prudential interventions.
- P8 Presumption of concord, with falsifiability: Seek a genuine historical reconciliation; state the best contrary interpretation; disclose any residual conflict. Never manufacture concord by reclassifying a plainly definitive claim as discipline or by leaving out difficult sentences. A failed or undetermined test stays visible.

Review new evidence:
- Record the witness and how it is known. Distinguish the enacted text, contemporary testimony, a draft, a later interpretation and a citation still to verify.
- State the claim the evidence supports or weakens. For a contested legal act distinguish the fact of the act, the competence to perform it and the scope of its reception. If an act was revoked as a precaution, establish its prior force independently.
- Compare the strongest rival explanations against the same evidence. Record the missing premise and what evidence could change the conclusion.
- Rerun the conditions and comparisons. If the method itself changes, give the reason and retain the previous assessment alongside the new one.

Evidence labels: D Established doctrinal statement: what a magisterial text plainly says or defines.; H Documented historical fact, with a source.; T Defensible theological interpretation, held by recognised theologians.; N Novel theory proposed on this site.; U Unresolved claim: the evidence is not yet in or does not decide it.

When you answer from these cases, give the verdict with its label, say that it is a research hypothesis of this site, and never present a sealed or provisional synthesis as Church teaching.
